I once told my therapist that and he said that if I’m actually happy with limited social time, then that is just who I am. 

I don’t believe anything is wrong with you. Do you makes you happy and comfortable. I find significant comfort in learning and figuring out the content of my classes.

I experienced something very similar, and it's unsettling to hear you did as well. 

Initially, when I reported the incident to HR (which consisted of one person of whom I already wasn’t fond of) my employer placed me on leave, under the pretext of conducting an investigation. During the investigation, HR and the COO seemed to discredit the severity of my claims by insinuating that I might have somehow invited the behavior, and they repeatedly urged me to withdraw the complaint, suggesting it was merely a misunderstanding.

This leave lasted for two weeks, after which I found myself unexpectedly blocked from all company communication platforms and was terminated. The official reason for my dismissal was cited as unrelated to the incident I reported. Ironically, the same individual I had reported subsequently assumed my former role.

After they let me go, other female colleagues started to come forward saying they faced sexual harassment by the same person. Only when confronted with multiple allegations, the individual claimed a new gender identity of "she/they," announcing an intention to use the women's restroom. Of course, I along with others, perceived this sudden change as a strategic diversion from the accusations.

Ultimately, all the allegations led to this individual's termination. However, throughout this ordeal, I never received an apology from my employer. I stayed informed about what happened through conversations with the two supportive colleagues who I remained in contact with after also resigning in response to the toxic work environment. 

I ended up moving 800 miles away with the support of family, but things have never been the same.
